question: The measures of the three angles of a triangle are in the ratio 17 : 13 : 15. Find the positive difference between the greatest and the smallest of these three angles.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total parts of the angles = 17 + 13 + 15 = 45 parts.

We know the sum of the interior angles of a triangle is always 180°.

45 parts = 180° ⇒ 1 part = 4°.

Difference between greatest (17) and smallest (13) angle parts = 17 − 13 = 4 parts.

Difference in degrees = 4 parts × 4° = 16°.

**∴ The correct answer is 16°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The measures of the three angles of a triangle are in the ratio 17 : 13 : 15.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of the interior angles of a triangle = 180°.

 17x + 13x + 15x = 180°

**Calculations:**

Let the exact values of the three angles be 17x, 13x, and 15x respectively.

⇒ 17x + 13x + 15x = 180°

⇒ 45x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 45

⇒ x = 4°

Now, calculate the values of the greatest and smallest angles:

The greatest angle = 17x = 17 × 4° = 68°.

The smallest angle = 13x = 13 × 4° = 52°.

⇒ Positive difference = Greatest angle − Smallest angle

⇒ 68° − 52° = 16°

**∴ The correct answer is 16°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles of any planar triangle is always exactly 180°.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote and non-adjacent interior angles.

Triangle Property related to Sides and Angles

In any triangle, the longest side is always positioned opposite the greatest interior angle, and the shortest side is opposite the smallest angle.
